Fourteen comments

This is the second tune in a set on John Williams first CD with The Reel with a Birl and Bothar na Sop. He plays these with Micho Russell.

↳ Posted by Thom Pratt on January 5th, 2002.

The Midnight Reel

Last in the opening set on the CD “Providence III”. I first heard this broadcast by Ronan Burke on his program Thar Droichead Sall on ClareFM ((http://www.clarefm.ie/main/progs/tradarchive.html). I was struck by the similarity in the first phrase of the A section to “The Merry Blacksmith” (https://thesession.org/tunes/72). It’s always easier to learn a tune that has sections that you already know! (Either that, or it becomes a brain teaser trying to keep them straight!)

↳ Posted by feadogboy on May 16th, 2006.

Alas, if I’m playing a tune with a phrase which occurs in another tune, I find it hard not to stray into the other tune!

Re: Mrs. Crotty’s Christening

One thing I like about this tune, at least the version by the Chieftains, is that excluding that long ‘d’ at the start of the tune, the first two and a half measures are like the first two of “The Bucks of Oranmore” played a beat later. It can sound a lot like “The Bucks” when you’re starting it, if you do it a certain way. I just think it’s interesting how some (possibly unrelated) tunes sound so similar when they go through transformations like this. Another pair I think of off-hand is “The Glen Allen” vs. “The Bag of Spuds” or (second part, at least) “Down the Broom”.

↳ Posted by Daniel Parker on October 21st, 2018.

Mrs. Crotty’s Christening, X:5

Played as a driving single reel in the ’70s by one or more of Tommy Peoples/Cathal McConnell/De Danann, my memory is hazy as to which (and I’ve forgotten how to put in grace notes, as well).
I enjoy dropping into the solid pulse of this after a more “floaty” tune ending on e, such as The Humours of Lissadel or Johnson’s.

Mrs. Crotty’s Christening, X:7

Based on Chieftains 2 , which has Michael Tubridy playing it on the concertina at the outset. They called it Mrs Crotty’s, who like MT was from Co. Clare. I guess MT heard her play it. This is, I believe, the earliest recording of the tune (1969) of those listed on The Session, and presumably where a lot of people first heard it.
